pdlmi

Documents/pdlmi

pdlmi stores finite YALMIP constraints generated from pdvar residual expressions. Inequalities use semidefinite meaning only when every original coefficient is square Hermitian; otherwise the whole inequality is entry-wise. Equality is direct coefficient equality and may be rectangular. Direct coefficient assembly is the default; Pólya degree elevation, fixed-order Putinar box assembly, and fixed-order full box Bernstein-Gram preordering are explicit alternatives.

DirectLPólyaL.applyPolya(p)PutinarL.applyPutinar()Full BoxL.applyFullBoxPreorder()

Direct

L

The default tests all three degree-two coefficients in each of the two physical cells.

Open the full Direct API reference →

Pólya

L.applyPolya(p)

Pólya elevation by p raises the Bernstein degree before the direct coefficient test.

Open the full Pólya API reference →

Putinar

L.applyPutinar()

For this one-parameter degree-two residual, the default order-one Markov–Lukács certificate uses two Gram blocks and three coefficient identities per cell. In two or more parameters, the Putinar module uses the unweighted term plus one axis-generator term at minimum order ceil(m/2).

Open the full Putinar API reference →

Full Box

L.applyFullBoxPreorder()

In one parameter the default full-box selector is the same order-one Markov–Lukács construction as Putinar.

Open the full Full Box API reference →

The four paths begin with the same stored residual. Direct tests every local coefficient and is the default. Pólya exactly elevates that residual before repeating the direct test. In one parameter, Putinar and Full box dispatch to the same parity-specific Markov–Lukács form with minimum order floor(m/2). In two or more parameters, Putinar uses an unweighted Gram term plus one generator-weighted term per axis at minimum ceil(m/2), while Full box includes every generator-subset product. Both Gram paths match exact box-polynomial identities. The SOS certificate chapter derives these ideas; the API pages below stay focused on callable syntax.

Implemented Behavior

Section titled “Implemented Behavior”

Version 0.4.7 assembles <=, >=, and == relations. Inequalities select one global semidefinite or entry-wise interpretation from all original coefficients. Equality is always direct and supports rectangular or non-Hermitian residuals. Direct coefficient-wise assembly is the default. Pólya assembly performs exact degree elevation before applying the coefficient test. Putinar and full-box assembly create independent positive-semidefinite Gram blocks for every physical cell and active rate row, together with exact Bernstein coefficient identities.

In one parameter, Putinar and full box share the parity-specific Markov–Lukács interval construction. For two or more parameters, Putinar uses an unweighted Gram term plus one term for each axis generator αs(1−αs)\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)αs​(1−αs​), while full box uses every subset product of those generators. Both select a fixed absolute order on each local hypercube. toYalmip concatenates the resulting finite constraints for an ordinary YALMIP solver call.

Properties

Section titled “Properties”

The constructor exposes private-set, read-only properties through dot access:

PropertyExampleMeaning
ConstraintsC.ConstraintsStored direct conditions, Gram-block conditions, and/or exact identities. May be empty for a proven equality.
ResidualC.ResidualPromoted lhs-rhs expression used to rebuild alternative inequality certificates.
RelationC.Relation"<=", ">=", or "==".
UsePolya, PolyaDegreeC.UsePolya, C.PolyaDegreePólya selector and degree increment.
UsePutinar, PutinarOrderC.UsePutinar, C.PutinarOrderPutinar selector and absolute order.
UseFullBoxPreorder, FullBoxOrderC.UseFullBoxPreorder, C.FullBoxOrderFull-box selector and absolute order.

Certificate selectors apply only to inequalities. Any selector on equality raises pdlmi:UnsupportedEqualityCertificate.

The SOS certificate map derives these coefficient and Gram constructions, including the one-dimensional Markov–Lukács form and the tensor box generators used in higher dimensions.
